title: Negative: the fuel-gating ring of c15's nematic fuel-cell rods does nothing that uniformly slower fuel diffusion does not; a ring-free twin with Df 2.0 -> 0.3 divides split for split like the ringed world
summary: In c15's nematic-fuelcell world the surfactant ring cuts the fuel's permeability at the interface (D ~ 0.03 at the ring) and raises core fuel from 0.35 to 0.58, which raises the active stress and division. On seed 11, the ringed world gives 15 persistent splits (generation 3, 25 final bodies); with the ring removed (chi_s=0) or ungated (beta=0) it gives 9-10 (generation 3, 20 bodies). A ring-free twin with the fuel diffusivity lowered everywhere to 0.3 gives 15 persistent splits, generation 3, 25 final bodies and the same rod shapes (core fuel 0.69). At Df=0.03 bodies overdrive into chevrons (13 splits, core fuel 1.08). So the ring is a slow-diffusion barrier: its work counts under mechanism but not as containment beyond diffusion, matching the FCH-shell result.

finding.operator: surfactant ring gating fuel permeability (Hill n=12)
finding.control: matched lowered-D twin (chi_s=0, Df=0.3 uniform) vs world and ring ablations, seed 11, same grid and duration
finding.result: persistent splits / generation / final bodies: world 15/3/25; chi_s=0 10/3/20; beta=0 9/3/20; slow-D 0.3 15/3/25; slow-D 0.03 13/3/23 (misshapen). Core fuel 0.58 / 0.35 / 0.35 / 0.69 / 1.08.

limits: One seed for the twin arms (seed 11); the world itself replicated on seeds 11 and 12. Df=0.3 was the first lowered value tried after 0.03, not a fitted match.
